title: Real elliptic-curve isogeny geometry under an arithmetic-only conditional null
proposition: On 38 frozen, genuine ecdata curves, compare within-conductor isogeny-label distance contrasts of the legacy ACSC coordinate map against an explicitly modified BSD-independent MCJ-inspired map.
falsifier: A class-label permutation null conditioned on conductor and rank may yield a primary map-contrast difference equal to or larger than the observed value; scale ablations and alternative selections could erase it.

sources: John Cremona ecdata allcurves/allcurves.00000-09999 at Git commit 25cec5ecfec8b9f016eb1631ac633194c2bed39f, entire file SHA-256 259f3846329395b371e8079c77a6f1097adaebc98a054974573e241416efa968; selected source line numbers preserved in curves.csv and result.json.
Exact classical Weierstrass b2/b4/b6/b8/c4/discriminant formulas; no BSD formula or observed cosmic data.

limitations: Small purposively selected conductor strata are not representative of ecdata or cosmology.
Original ACSC rank is an isogeny invariant; rank-conditioned null is necessary to avoid tautological advantage, but does not control every arithmetic dependency.
Modified MCJ includes torsion instead of Im(log j) to avoid degeneracy for rational j and is not the exact manuscript formula.
Euclidean distance and scaling are imposed, not derived physical metrics; no galaxy or cosmological outcomes are used.
No independent scientific review, theorem proof, observed physical correspondence or upstream eligibility is asserted.
